thompson1917-ch02-01: W = kL^3; form unchanged during growth \iff k constant
thompson1917-ch02-02: d \propto h^{3/2} (no buckling under own weight); h_{max} \approx 300\,\text{ft} for the Kew-flagstaff pine

thompson1917-ch02-09: impulse \propto M \Rightarrow v_0 independent of L; jump height h = v_0^2/2g independent of L
thompson1917-ch02-10: V \propto L^{1/2} for swimming (Froude), flight (minimum speed) and walking (pendulum leg)
thompson1917-ch02-12: S/M \approx \text{const} maintained by change of form, against S/M \propto L^{-1} for similar forms
thompson1917-ch02-15: cell division keeps S/M \approx \text{const}; cleavage increases S at constant V and M
thompson1917-ch03-07: W \propto L^3 whatever the law of growth L(t)

thompson1917-ch03-21: v(\theta + n) = x^n v(\theta) for a rise of n degrees; temperature coefficient of growth x^{10} \approx 2\text{--}3
thompson1917-ch03-23: L(t) = \bar{L}(t) + A(t)\sin(2\pi t / 1\,\text{yr}), A(t) \to 0 as d\bar{L}/dt \to 0 (damped sine)
thompson1917-ch03-30: V^m T^n = \text{const}; for regenerating tadpole tails V T^2 \approx \text{const}
thompson1917-ch05-10: 1/r_1 + 1/r_2 = \text{const}; surfaces of revolution: plane, sphere, cylinder, catenoid, unduloid, nodoid

thompson1917-ch05-24: biconcave corpuscle: 1/r_1 + 1/r_2 \neq \text{const}, so not a fluid drop in equilibrium under surface tension alone
thompson1917-ch07-02: fluid partition meets a rigid wall at 90^\circ (Sachs's rule)
thompson1917-ch07-04: walls meet three at a time at 120^\circ, independent of cell size; relative sizes set only wall curvature
thompson1917-ch07-06: T_{cc} > T_{cm} \Rightarrow external angle < 120^\circ; T_{cc} \ge T_{cm} + T'_{cm} \Rightarrow contact only at a point
thompson1917-ch07-09: uniform pressure on similar cylinders or spheres \Rightarrow hexagons, 6 neighbours, angles 120^\circ
thompson1917-ch07-11: hexagonal prism closed by three rhombic facets at 109^\circ 28' (\cos\theta = -1/3); minimal surface for given volume

thompson1917-ch08-02: partition \Sigma = \arg\min |\Sigma| subject to dividing V in the given ratio
thompson1917-ch08-03: unequal division of a cube: quarter-cylinder in a corner minimal for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.3; spherical octant for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.15
thompson1917-ch08-04: bisecting a quadrant: circular arc \perp side and periphery, cutting off 55^\circ 22' of the arc, starting \approx 0.3r from the centre
thompson1917-ch08-05: sector cell divides anticlinally iff 62\tfrac{1}{2}^\circ \lesssim \theta \le 90^\circ, otherwise periclinally
thompson1917-ch08-06: after bisecting a quadrant: triangular cell reaches division size at 1.345r, quadrilateral at 1.517r
thompson1917-ch08-09: n cells meeting three at a time with a common outer boundary need n - 3 partitions; n = 8 gives 13 types
thompson1917-ch09-08: spicule follows a geodesic of the cell surface: \kappa_g = 0
thompson1917-ch09-10: three equal cells \Rightarrow triradiate spicule, rays at 120^\circ; four cells \Rightarrow tetraradiate, rays at \approx 109^\circ 28'
thompson1917-ch09-16: six plane interfaces meeting in threes at 120^\circ; edges meeting at \approx 109^\circ 28'
thompson1917-ch10-01: geodesics on a cylinder of radius r: circles z = c, lines \theta = c, helices z = a\theta
thompson1917-ch10-02: spiral geodesic on a right cone (\kappa_g = 0) coils more closely as the cone narrows
thompson1917-ch10-04: fibre fixed at both ends on a curved surface takes the shortest path: \kappa_g = 0
thompson1917-ch11-03: constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}, the ratio fixing \alpha; \alpha = 90^\circ circle, \alpha \to 0 straight line
thompson1917-ch11-04: successive shoots l_{n+1} = q\,l_n at equal angles are tangents to r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

thompson1917-ch11-06: each increment G is a gnomon: F \cup G \sim F
thompson1917-ch11-10: \alpha \approx 80^\circ in Nautilus (b_{n+1}/b_n \approx 3); usually 80^\circ \le \alpha \le 85^\circ in ammonitoid and gastropod shells
thompson1917-ch11-16: r(\theta, t) = t\,f(\theta) from the umbo; f(\theta) = \cos\theta gives coaxial circles
thompson1917-ch12-04: r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}, recognised by self-similarity of young and old shells

thompson1917-ch13-03: v_1/v_2 = \text{const} on opposite sides of the axis \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}
thompson1917-ch13-06: plane spiral iff the maximal and minimal growth rates around the base lie at \Delta\phi = 180^\circ; otherwise helicospiral
thompson1917-ch13-13: unequal longitudinal growth by permanent increments \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

thompson1917-ch14-09: conspicuous parastichies set by the ratio of the diagonals of the rhomboid circumscribing each leaf-area, not by the divergence angle

thompson1917-ch15-11: t(1/r + 1/r') = C within each cavity of the heart
thompson1917-ch15-15: \cos x = L/L', L and L' the energy loss per unit length in trunk and branch
thompson1917-ch16-04: wall thickness t(x) \propto bending moment M(x), maximal at mid-shaft
thompson1917-ch16-05: trabeculae lie along the principal stress trajectories \sigma_1, \sigma_2, crossing at 90^\circ
thompson1917-ch16-10: height of vertebral spine h(x) \propto bending moment M(x)
thompson1917-ch16-14: three series of processes at \approx 120^\circ to one another

thompson1917-ch17-06: (x, y) \mapsto (x, cy): at equal length c \approx 2/3 (sheep), c \approx 1/3 (giraffe) relative to ox
thompson1917-ch17-08: \theta' = k\theta for angles to equal radii on the two halves of the leaf
